html:
The All-India Muslim League was the political party that spoke for Muslims in British India. It was founded at Dhaka in 1906, and under Muhammad Ali Jinnah it won the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

It grew from Muslim landowners, princes and graduates of Aligarh college, who feared that a Hindu majority would swamp Muslims as the Raj opened elected councils. At first it stood for loyalty to Britain and separate electorates for Muslims, which it won in 1909. For a time it worked with the Indian National Congress, in the Lucknow Pact of 1916.

In 1930 its president, the poet Muhammad Iqbal, proposed a Muslim state in northwest India. The League did badly in the 1937 elections, and Jinnah rebuilt it. In the Lahore Resolution of 1940 it demanded independent states for the Muslim-majority regions. It swept the Muslim seats in the elections of 1946, and its call for Direct Action that August set off riots in Calcutta. A united India no longer seemed possible, and partition followed in August 1947. The party then split into Pakistani and Indian successors.
sum: The All-India Muslim League was the political party that spoke for Muslims in British India. It was founded at Dhaka in 1906, and under Muhammad Ali Jinnah it won the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
